Text 1

Oil extraction and other human activities are sources of atmospheric methane (CH4), but, as Donald Wuebbles and Katherine Hayhoe have shown, so too are naturally occurring emissions, such as those from termite mounds. This biogenic CH4 is challenging to track given natural sources' variability and spatial diffusion, but one promising approach is to use CH4 flux data from extant monitoring infrastructure as proxies for CH4 fluxes in unmonitored areas.

Text 2

Sparkle Malone and colleagues examined the United States' network of eddy covariance (EC) towers—the equipment used to track CH4 fluxes—to evaluate the utility of network data for quantifying biogenic CH4. KING HENRY: My blood hath been too cold and temperate, Unapt to stir at these indignities, And you have found me, for accordingly You tread upon my patience; but be sure I will from henceforth rather be myself, Mighty and to be fear'd, than my [disposition], Which hath been smooth as oil, soft as young down, And therefore lost that title of respect Which the proud soul ne'er pays but to the proud.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Marta Danielsdottir et al.'s 2007 study of planktonic ecosystems used a nutrient-phytoplankton-zooplankton (NPZ) model.
  • Diane Stoecker et al. (2017): NPZ models rely "on the differentiation of the planktonic communities into phytoplankton or zooplankton, functional types," excluding mixotrophic plankton.
  • Phytoplankton are exclusively phototrophic, producing nutrients via photosynthesis.
  • Zooplankton are exclusively phagotrophic, obtaining nutrients by consuming other organisms.
  • Many plankton are mixotrophic, meaning that they combine phototrophic and phagotrophic functions.

questions.stem: A student wants to undermine a scientific assumption about magma chambers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.html: Scientists found inactive Cascade Range volcanoes with large magma chambers below their surface, challenging the theory that magma chambers only exist right before eruptions.
Researchers detected magma chambers by tracking earthquake waves through partially melted rock, improving volcano monitoring and eruption prediction methods for dormant volcanoes.
Magma chambers need over 35% liquid rock to potentially erupt, refuting the assumption that volcanoes dormant for thousands of years have melted rock below.
The magma chambers discovered beneath inactive Cascade Range volcanoes are located 3 to 9 miles below the volcanoes' surfaces, indicating that such chambers can occur at varying depths underground.

  • Magma chambers need over 35% liquid rock to potentially erupt.
